description: A parenthesized FROM join - FROM ( a JOIN b ON c ). The parentheses are PURE GROUPING: the query is identical to FROM a JOIN b ON c and, unlike a derived-table subquery, the inner table ALIASES stay visible to the outer WHERE and SELECT. The engine flattens the grouping into the ordinary join pipeline, recursively, so ((a JOIN b) JOIN c) works too, and a grouped chain may be the RIGHT side of an outer join - the inner chain executes first and its aliases join the outer scope, so the outer ON can reference them. The regression that goes with the grammar alternative is here as well: the (SELECT ...) derived-table form must keep parsing. Converted 1:1 from query/ParenthesizedFromJoinTest (now retired); the equivalence test looped over two result sets, so the converted test pins the ordered rows of both spellings, and the COUNT(*)-only tests keep the count and add the rows behind it.
